name: Griffith-Sowers House

location.text: Rowan County, near Salisbury, North Carolina

dates.note: The NC nomination: 'When built in ca.1930-1932'; the Wikipedia infobox: 'Built 1930', architect Percy Bloxam; the node's year is 1932.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 09000703; added September 9, 2009 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: Read from the Wikipedia infobox, not from the National Register's own database, which was not opened for this building.

refs.title: Griffith-Sowers House, Salisbury vicinity, Rowan County, RW0971, Listed 9/9/2009 -- North Carolina State Historic Preservation Office nomination by Davyd Foard Hood
refs.note: The nomination's description: 'a large, flush-sheathed, two-story-with-attic frame Colonial Revival-style country house' with 'a five-part plan composed of a dominant five-bay wide center block, covered by a side-gable roof, that is linked by shallow one-bay wide hyphens to its flanking, recessed, perpendicular gable-front two-story wings, which are two bays in width'; 'The main block, just under fifty feet in width'; 'The south-facing façade ... is eleven bays wide'; 'covered with a slate roof' on 'a common bond brick foundation'.

refs.title: Griffith-Sowers House Rowan County, NC (Rowan County Historic Landmarks Commission report)

note: Written 4 Sep 2026. No HABS; the nomination is the measured document and it describes a FRAME house with flush sheathing, called Colonial Revival by its author -- worth knowing on a node whose prose is about Flemish-bond brick, a water table and a belt course. The five-part plan and the just-under-fifty-foot centre block are the nomination's figures and live in its ref note, not in a survey block, because they are not HABS's.
